v2Additions: ai-platform-descriptor/v2 (declarative platform identity + capability facets, replaces schema platform enum)

dependencies.note: Must not depend on runner or repo-lint implementations (no circular dependency). Consumers pin this version.

entryVersionResolution: prepare.target.version optional; entry alias literal 'current' resolved once by the engine in the order explicit > platform-default override > shared current and pinned exact with provenance (wf-runner >= 0.7.4)
additionsIn120: ai-run-lock/v1.2: execution.rigor (fast|balanced|full), execution.gated, execution.frozen, execution.execPath, execution.hostConsent, execution.environmentSealed
ai-run-lock/v1.2 rules: frozen=true requires rigor=full and gated=true; execPath=host-controlled requires hostConsent; environmentSealed=false requires an empty selection.environment
selection.environment minItems relaxed from 1 to 0 (D-27: a platform with no sealed script environment can now write a legal lock)
ai-run-protocol/v1.3: a prepare response may carry the first claim (result.task + reason=claimed), which is what lets rigor=fast run a single round trip; a claimed response without a task is invalid
v1.1 locks and v1.1/v1.2 protocol documents remain valid: every change is additive
additionsIn121: prepare request may declare rigor (fast|balanced|full) - $defs.prepare is additionalProperties:false, so an undeclared tier could not be sent at all
prepare request may declare consent (agreement text + optional grantedAt), the only lawful way for a run to be allowed host-controlled script execution

tiers stay cost-only by contract: no rule here keys any capability off rigor, because BP-2 makes the capability floor identical in all three (a fast run keeps every function, it keeps less evidence). The lock-level tie-rules in 1.2.0 carry the whole restriction: frozen requires full+gated.

a fast prepare may answer with the first claim in the same envelope; that is why 1.2.0 added the v1.3 rule "a prepare response whose reason is claimed must carry a task". Under v1.1/v1.2 a fast run simply gets the two round trips it always got.
additionsIn122: handoff-bundle.schema.json (handoff-bundle/v1): the platform-neutral交接包 shape BP-4 §4.5 names as the only cross-run state channel - completed-stage conclusions (common $defs/completion, so digests are the same objects a submit carries), a *version view* with no host paths, the artifact rows the bundle directory must contain, and an integrity digest over them.

state.schema.json rule 2 narrowed, not loosened: "prepared => completed is empty" now holds for every run **except** one whose state names the run and bundle manifest it was imported from (x-handoff.fromRun + manifestSha256). A run that imported nothing still cannot start with a filled completed list - checked below in both directions.
no protocol change: prepare/stop already accept ^x- payload keys, so a bundle is requested through x-handoff and never through a new operation or a new protocol version.
a bundle always describes finished stages of some other run: it cannot carry an in-flight state machine, and a continuing run re-pins versions in its own lock (2.1.0 §3.6 red line).
